title: Sunny and the Little Gecko | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka spots a tiny gecko clinging upside-down to a moonlit bark, completely unbothered by gravity, and wonders what the world must look like from up there. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
There was a gecko on the bark.

Not on top of the bark — on the underside of a piece of loose stringybark that had peeled and curled away from the trunk. Upside-down. Completely upside-down, clinging there as easily as Sunny stood on the ground.

She tilted her head.

The gecko tilted its head.

It was very small — small enough to fit in her palm with room to spare. Its skin was pale and almost translucent in the moonlight, and its eyes were enormous — round and dark and bright, taking up most of its tiny face. It watched her with great calm.

She wondered what the world looked like from up there. Upside-down. The ground above, the sky below.

The gecko flicked its tiny tongue.

It shifted a little, its toe pads gripping the bark without effort. Each tiny toe had invisible hairs so fine they could cling to anything — she'd heard that once and never forgotten it. A gecko could walk up glass. A gecko found the world a perfectly walkable place in every direction.

She envied it, a little.

She sat down on the soft earth and looked up at it.

The gecko looked back down at her.

They stayed like that for a long time — one upside-down, one right-way-up — until Sunny's eyes grew soft and heavy.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little gecko. Goodnight, little one.
